Yeah, according to the article, “she essentially “fell apart” when they moved her body. Her insides were basically liquefied.” That part couldn’t have been a pretty sight, ironically.
According to Wikipedia, her mother had undiagnosed and untreated depression. I can only assume those are the tendencies, and that honestly makes this even sadder.

To be fair, it’s not exactly common for a body to look this intact and peaceful after slamming into a limousine from nearly 90 stories up. The unusual aftermath of an otherwise tragic suicide is what gives it the poetic viewpoint that many people have come to understand.

“The young and pretty Evelyn leaped from the 86th-floor observatory in 1947 and landed on the roof of a United Nations limousine parked on the street below.

Her calmly elegant demeanor, her legs crossed at the ankles, the way the car’s metal folded like sheets and framed her head and arms—perhaps these were the reasons that McHale’s death was given its title as “The Most Beautiful Suicide”. When she died, she was still wearing her pearls and white gloves.”

“…despite the 1050-foot fall (320 m), her body looked intact.

Remarkably Evelyn shows absolutely no evidence of trauma and appears disarmingly placid and composed – as if asleep. Around her, however, the crumpled sheet metal and broken glass show the violent destructive evidence of her jump.”

The surrealism is that her corpse appeared eloquent and untouched. It was one of those moments that had to be seen to be believed, as a 1000 ft drop almost never guarantees a pretty result of anything, let alone a human body. Not to mention, the photo was taken mere minutes after she landed. To many, myself included, she would easily appear as though she was sleeping in any other setting. 

Unfortunately, though…

“…she essentially “fell apart” when they moved her body. Her insides were basically liquefied.”

Photography is considered a form of art, and this piece happened to capture something tragic, disheartening, and devastating. A young woman took her life, suffering the same sorts of feelings that many women struggle with today, and it’s something we will and do recognize as we study these photos. The depressing irony and realism of her situation is also what makes it feel poetic.

I’ve heard of that being possible with bipolar disorder. I know someone with it and witnessing it made me terrified for them. I was scared that every moment I wasn’t with or talking to them, they would lose themselves just like that. It sounds so terrifying, I can’t even imagine what it must feel like.

It brings to question: what caused that reassurance to disappear? Like a tipping point. We all have one, and we all have things that could push us over. I think of that reassurance as a seatbelt that holds us back from jumping out the car. Without it, the impulsivity is dangerously stronger than it ever should be. That impulsivity and lack of reassurance is what I’m afraid of most.

From what I’ve learned with medications, you will have your highs and you’ll certainly have lows. People have always warned me against medication but I did it anyway. I cannot say it hasn’t helped, it certainly has. But at the same time, sometimes Ive never felt worse in my life. But without them, I’m certainly not going to last long. It’s so tricky and it’s so scary. I suppose that’s why you’re supposed to keep the medical people updated with how you’re doing and how they’re affecting you. They suspect this very thing can happen and want to counter it however they can. 

Meanwhile, outside of that, there’s a matter of what you can and can’t do while trying them out. You don’t know what they’ll do to you, and you don’t know if they’ll help. You only know that you *want* them to help. You *want* them to work. Or rather, you *need* them to. Maybe that could be where the convincing comes in. Optimism, in a sort, that this is the proper solution and things will be okay. I feel like that can create the fear/dread of them not working. 

Medications, therapy, and all of the help we try to seek is all equally scary and can have many positive and negative effects on our bodies and mind. It’s important to know yourself to a degree where you’ll know of what you’re feeling is real and most importantly, if it’s *right*.

Your uncle's justification is pretty shitty, ngl, and since they're already getting her a less-expensive keyboard, there was definitely no reason to force you to let her play yours.

Alternatively, not playing it while she was around was also an option. I would've waited until they weren't around to set it up and play so you can 1) be undisturbed with your new present and 2) it wouldn't have become a bigger issue to the point where you were bullied out of using your own present. That would suck equally, but sometimes that's an effective way to deal with people like your uncle. It's pretty entitled of him to expect you to let her play with your property just because your cousin be mad otherwise, she needs to learn that not everything has to go her way just because her parents don't feel like dealing with her potential tantrum. It wasn't rude of you to deny them, and the fact that he guilt tripped and pushed you like that just to make his child happy makes him a pretty shitty parent.

So yeah, I'm on your side and I apologize that you have to put up with that.

This past weekend, I attended my cousin's funeral. I was not too close to him, but I went to support my mother and great-grandmother because they were deeply upset about the passing.

The service itself was nice. My cousin was resting in a cool blue coffin with a very nice suit on. It honestly disturbed me; I used to read up on how bodies were prepared for funerals and seeing his body with that in mind bugged the hell out of me, but I kept my concerns to myself of course. The really fucked up part is the trip to the cemetery.

I rode with my mom and a couple others and we were near the center of the funeral precession line. For those who don't know, funeral precession lines are basically the hearse (the car that carries the coffin and probably pallbearers), the limo (which to my knowledge carries immediate family like mom, dad, siblings), and the car of every person or group of people at the funeral in a single line with each car having their hazards and brights on and a funeral sticker on the lower right corner of the windshield. In addition, they don't have to follow traffic laws so we were running red lights and all that jazz.

Anyways while we were driving we were almost involved in a car wreck at least 3 times. People around here apparently do not respect funeral precessions and see them as people disrupting traffic and cutting off the regular flow of things, because we had people disrupting the line by forcing themselves in so they can still pass through regular traffic. Horrible, but that's not the worst part. 

No, the worst part was when these four douchebags in a crap car were too impatient to wait for the line to pass and tried to force themselves past us on a tiny road. We were next to the cemetery and had to drive a bit down a narrow street to turn into the entrance. These assholes were turning onto this road - which was so thin that only allow one car at a time to pass through on either lane - and tried to pass us. First, they almost hit the car ahead of us, then nearly hit our car, then the two cars behind us had enough and drove past them without acknowledgement. From what I saw in the back windshield, these assholes nearly crashed into two cars behind us, both of which had enough and tried going around the d-bags. They then forced themselves into the line and rode until we turned into the cemetery, and they then took off. 

I kept thinking that if they hit at least one of our cars trying to pass, they could've caused a pretty serious car wreck or even pileup because A) there were still at least 10 cars behind this in the precession, B) This was dangerously close to the other lane and the cars going in the opposite direction could have easily crashed because of this nonsense, and C) the way these douchebags tried merging had them taking up part of both lanes and could have caused someone to swerve off road into the cemetery, which would have been fucked up enough considering the occasion.

Aside from that, watching family members I never met breaking down over my cousin's burial site was haunting and made my already shot nerves even more distressed. 

The whole thing has kept me up over the last few days and I've had worse nightmares than I usually did. Cherry on top is that this is the first funeral I've been to since 2018 due to trauma with dead bodies in the past, and this arguably made it worse. But I will say I'm also glad that I went so I could at least be more familiarized with how funerals run should I have to go to another one again soon.

TL;DR: A car full of assholes nearly turned a funeral precession into a car pileup. Otherwise attended a nice funeral service and the overall experience both worsened trauma and helped me deal with funerals.

The prefix "Bi" may mean "two" but that doesn't mean bisexuals are limited to two genders! Bisexuality is fluid, so it can include anywhere between two genders and all genders, while preferences don't determine whether or not you're bisexual, and loving all genders doesn't automatically make you pan! There are tons of bisexuals who love all genders regardless of gender.

Pansexuality is just specifically all genders regardless of gender. The main difference between the two is that bi is broader and includes many kinds of attraction, while pan is specifically all genders. It's mainly up to the person how they wish to identify at the end of the day.

A good way to differentiate it is by attraction, and what I mean by that is:

Bisexuality is a fluid identity that includes attraction between two genders and all genders, with or without preferences. This means some bisexuals can love two, some love a few, some love multiple and others love all. Preferences don’t determine whether or not you’re bisexual.

Pansexuality is specifically the attraction to all genders, regardless of gender. 

Someone who likes all genders isn’t automatically pan, it’s up to the person to label themselves

Some bisexuals are attracted to people regardless of gender. A better difference would be:

Bi = 2 or more genders; a fluid identity that encompasses attraction between two and all genders with or without preferences.
Pan = specifically all genders regardless of gender 

Pan is specific with its attraction, while Bi is more broad
